correctness.rationale: An exact two-copy assignment proof establishes the integer interval of admissible one-one roots, with all zero-gap boundaries; six bound comparisons reduce R≥r to four gap inequalities. The three-gap subtraction by 2(r-1) is a bijection onto the r=1 language of half-length m-3(r-1), whose independent finite sum is 1+3 binom(h,2). Tail differencing, maximal r and the limiting mixture law follow algebraically. The independent dynamic-programming checker passed all 946 gap words for m≤11, and independent direct gap enumerations through m=64. These computations corroborate rather than prove the infinite claim.

value.rationale: The inverse counting of distinct roots per shuffle square is a published motivated question. A complete fiber-size distribution for a natural fixed-Hamming-weight family, with a direct gap-trimming bijection and nondegenerate limiting law, adds information not supplied by the established recognition total or forward root-generation count. The exact result holds at all lengths and can serve as a baseline for higher-Hamming-weight multiplicity questions.
